Class IndexWriter

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.build.IndexWriter
public final class IndexWriter extends Object
Builds the bytes of MICRONAUT-INF/index.bin from a description of the jars and entries a runner jar contains.

The writer derives everything the format requires from the entry names: the multi-release aliases of a jar flagged IndexFormat.JAR_FLAG_MULTI_RELEASE, the synthetic records for directories that are implied but never stored, the chain of records that share a logical name, and the open addressed hash table that finds a chain in one probe. See IndexFormat for the layout it writes.

Why this is a two step API

Every record of the index is fixed size and the string table holds names, not offsets, so the length of the index depends only on how many jars, entries and packages there are and on what they are called. It does not depend on the offsets the index stores. layout() exploits that: it lays the index out and reports its IndexWriter.Layout.length() before a single byte of the archive has been written. The packager can then place the index entry in the outer archive, learn where every entry after it will land, feed those offsets back into the specs and call write(Layout, long). Without that property the archive would have to be written twice.

IndexWriter writer = new IndexWriter().startClass("com.example.Application");
IndexWriter.JarSpec application = writer.addJar(IndexFormat.CLASSES_PREFIX);
IndexWriter.EntrySpec entry = application.addEntry("com/example/Application.class");
IndexWriter.Layout layout = writer.layout();
// ... place an index of layout.length() bytes in the archive, then:
entry.dataOffset(offsetOfThatEntry);
byte[] index = writer.write(layout, archiveLength);

This is build time code: it is written as ordinary Java, unlike the reader in the launcher.

    • addJar

      public IndexWriter.JarSpec addJar(String name)
      Adds a jar. The first jar added is the application layer, jar 0, and is flagged IndexFormat.JAR_FLAG_IS_OUTER.
      Parameters:
      name - the jar name: MICRONAUT-INF/lib/<file>.jar, or IndexFormat.CLASSES_PREFIX for the application layer
      Returns:
      the jar, to describe its entries and metadata with
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if name is null
      IllegalStateException - if the format's jar limit would be exceeded

    • layout

      public IndexWriter.Layout layout()
      Lays the index out: expands the aliases and synthetic directories, chains the records that share a name, sizes and fills the hash table and builds the string table.

      Nothing here reads an offset, which is exactly the point: the resulting IndexWriter.Layout.length() is the final length of the index, so the caller can reserve room for it and only then work out where everything else in the archive lands.

      Returns:
      the layout, to be handed back to write(Layout, long)
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if a name is too long for the format, or the hash table cannot be filled within IndexFormat.MAX_PROBE_LIMIT probes

    • write

      public byte[] write(IndexWriter.Layout layout, long outerFileLength)
      Writes the index.

      Offsets and sizes are read from the specs as they stand now, so this is the call that picks up whatever the packager learned about the archive after layout() ran. The layout itself, and therefore the length of the result, is unchanged.

      Parameters:
      layout - the layout this writer produced
      outerFileLength - the length of the finished outer archive, which the reader checks against the file it opens
      Returns:
      the complete index, exactly IndexWriter.Layout.length() bytes long
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if layout is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the layout belongs to another writer, or a value does not fit the field the format stores it in
